pr_title: Add a config to MIBC format
pr_body:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/523221/176061310-22016b7c-fddb-4967-bc60-446a0a1da995.png)

pr_comments: Let me know if I e.g. should serialize it to e.g. JSON or CSV and put into a single `ldstr` or if there is a way to write the whole thing to a sort of manifest and stuff like that.

One could also serialize this info as custom attributes. The ldstr/pop and ldtoken/pop is used for the rest of the MIBC stuff because it's more compact than custom attributes. We don't care about compactness for metadata that much. Custom attributes look nicer when looked at in e.g. ilspy. One could use [AssemblyMetadataAttribute](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.reflection.assemblymetadataattribute.-ctor?view=net-6.0#system-reflection-assemblymetadataattribute-ctor(system-string-system-string)) from mscorlib so that it even nicely resolves to something.

But not sure if it's a scenario we need to optimize for and you already wrote the code to use ldstr/pop...

@mdh1418 We should extend ClrEtwAll.man with the new enum values as well as strings. Since this PR has been merged, we need do it in separate PR.

Once we have the [ClrEtwAll.man](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/coreclr/vm/ClrEtwAll.man) extended, we should also make sure perfview and EventTrace library correctly handles the new enum value. @brianrob can guide you through the steps needed to update these libraries in order to align to extensions to ClrEtwAll.man.

issue_context.title: Include runtime flavor and platform information into .mibc Profile
issue_context.body:
With the work to [enable PGO-based Profiled AOT on Mono](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/69512), mono based .mibc files can now be generated. It would be convenient if there was some way to identify the Runtime flavor, Platform OS + Arch for a corresponding .mibc file. 

For instance, I had been testing the full pipeline of Profiled AOT on Mono, but unknowingly had generated a coreclr based .mibc (probably accidentally published a coreclr build and collected a .nettrace from the resulting executable). Only after comparing with another `.mibc` that is more clearly Mono based could we guess that the previous .mibc was a coreclr based one.

/cc: @lambdageek @davidwrighton @lateralusX @tommcdon
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Issue Details
With the work to [enable PGO-based Profiled AOT on Mono](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/69512), mono based .mibc files can now be generated. It would be convenient if there was some way to identify the Runtime flavor, Platform OS + Arch for a corresponding .mibc file. For instance, I had been testing the full pipeline of Profiled AOT on Mono, but unknowingly had generated a coreclr based .mibc (probably accidentally published a coreclr build and collected a .nettrace from the resulting executable). Only after comparing with another `.mibc` that is more clearly Mono based could we guess that the previous .mibc was a coreclr based one. /cc: @lambdageek @davidwrighton @lateralusX
Author: mdh1418
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-Diagnostics-coreclr`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

There are a couple of subtasks here:
* Extend the mibc format to include optional runtime information - at the very least profile platform/architecture and runtime flavor (coreclr vs mono vs ...).  For example I wonder if collecting a profile on coreclr x64 and deploying to arm64 is worth at least a warning.
* Extend the information in .nettrace files (rundown?) to include platform info and runtime flavor.
* Make changes to the `dotnet-pgo` tool to shovel the platform info from .nettrace to .mibc

I don't think we necessarily want a profile to become unusable if it's from the "wrong" runtime/platform, but it would be easier to diagnose profile issues if there was an option for the runtime to report that profile XYZ doesn't match platform/runtime ABC

I planned to try to extend the MIBC format too, was planning to add:
1) versioning
2) "is it app specific or some common profile" flag
3) working set size
Adding @davidwrighton @mangod9 who own the mibc format

This seems pretty good. Adding an extra method to the PGO data to encode this data should be straightforward. I'd like to see it structured as a key/value store. Probably with just strings for keys and values.

> There are a couple of subtasks here:
> 
> * Extend the mibc format to include optional runtime information - at the very least profile platform/architecture and runtime flavor (coreclr vs mono vs ...).  For example I wonder if collecting a profile on coreclr x64 and deploying to arm64 is worth at least a warning.
> * Extend the information in .nettrace files (rundown?) to include platform info and runtime flavor.
> * Make changes to the `dotnet-pgo` tool to shovel the platform info from .nettrace to .mibc

When closing a session there is a process info event emitted, it includes command line, os  info as well as CPU architecture, but currently not runtime flavor.

> I planned to try to extend the MIBC format too, was planning to add:
> 
> 1. versioning
> 2. "is it app specific or some common profile" flag
> 3. working set size

@EgorBo has agreed to take a look at adding the runtime flavor info to the MIBC file format.  @EgorBo please let me know if any help/assistance is need with adding the runtime flavor to the process info event.

> When closing a session there is a process info event emitted, it includes command line, os info as well as CPU architecture, but currently not runtime flavor.

Thanks, I see `ProcessInfo` event that contains OS and Arch.

> Adding an extra method to the PGO data to encode this data should be straightforward. I'd like to see it structured as a key/value store. Probably with just strings for keys and values.

@davidwrighton do you mean like
```
ldstr "key1"
ldstr "value1"
pop
pop
ldstr "key2"
ldstr "value2"
pop
pop
...
```
?

review_comments: How does the Sku work (what does it stand for)? It would be nice to have the mono runtime be emitted, so if we use the Sku for emitting runtime, would it be unproblematic to extend the Sku enum to also contain Mono (not sure if there is a trickle effect)? What is the `Runtime/Start` event/where do i look to find it?

I wasn't sure what to pick for runtime so probably it would be easier if you tell me which event to analyze cc @lateralusX
I just opened a random nettrace via PerfView and searched for CoreCLR - this was the first thing to pop up - I assume mono runtime is expected to send this exact event on start with a different value for Sku

If that eventname is the same as `FireEtwRuntimeInformationDCStart`, it seems to be the right event. I think we can try adding mono to the Sku Enum, right now we are emitting CoreCLR as well on Mono https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/41d9c1cc0dca16743a54971930e81d60777af746/src/mono/mono/eventpipe/ep-rt-mono.c#L2804 since it wasn't clear whether a non 0x1, 0x2 Sku value will cause problems anywhere that its used.
I don't see `FireEtwRuntimeInformationDCStart` in my sample nettrace
Here is the events we collect - `Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime:0x1F000080018:5`

So judging by the code `FireEtwRuntimeInformationDCStart ` is a mono function that sends the event I parse. So I assume the task is to extend Sku to include Mono, because currently Mono sends "CoreCLR"

FireEtwRuntimeInformationDCStart is fired as part of rundown, meaning that it will go into every session that gets closed and have requested rundown events (most tools always request rundown events). Currently Mono uses the same Sku enum value as CoreCLR, and was kept that way to not introduce any potential issues in tooling and so far, no need to differentiate the value. If we would like to use the Sku and add a Mono enum value to it, we would need to validate that tools consuming nettrace files are still capable to handle the generated Mono nettrace file (like perfview, TraceEvent library etc).
@lateralusX so, just tell me which exact event to check to detect mono runtime? 🙂

I extended the Sku Enum to have Mono 0x4 in both `src/coreclr/inc/eventtracebase.h` and `src/coreclr/nativeaot/Runtime/eventtracebase.h`
```
typedef enum _Sku
{
    DesktopCLR=0x1,
    CoreCLR=0x2,
    Mono=0x4
}Sku;
```
and the generated .nettrace is still compatible with perfview and visual studio (as in no throws or crashes from viewing the .nettrace). The only catch is that the value of Sku is literal `Sku="4"` compared to `Sku="CoreClr"` and `Sku="DesktopClr"`. I believe that is because the libraries define the Sku as `RuntimeSku` with only enum vars for 0x1 and 0x2. https://github.com/microsoft/perfview/blob/8f5c46ad3980ecbd8845bff274911ecb22f98f3f/src/TraceEvent/Parsers/ClrEtwAll.cs.base#L6902-L6906

I'm not sure if there are other tooling or more advanced usages of .nettrace Rundown Runtime/Start events that leverage the value of Sku, but if this is the only extent, then it looks like we are good to go to with using the event.

@EgorBo can we include extending the Sku in this PR? 
```
typedef enum _Sku
{
    DesktopCLR=0x1,
    CoreCLR=0x2,
    Mono=0x4
}Sku;
```
in both `src/coreclr/inc/eventtracebase.h` and `src/coreclr/nativeaot/Runtime/eventtracebase.h`
and changing the 
`#define RUNTIME_SKU_CORECLR 0x2` to `#define RUNTIME_SKU_MONO 0x4` https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ade0b2146555e19bc77f1c7e8e36da40bcb7fc3a/src/mono/mono/eventpipe/ep-rt-mono.c#L153
as well as the rundown event Sku value
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ade0b2146555e19bc77f1c7e8e36da40bcb7fc3a/src/mono/mono/eventpipe/ep-rt-mono.c#L2804
to be `RUNTIME_SKU_MONO`

We are discussing extending the sku to include Mono, probably as value 3 since that is the next available value, but just make sure you get the sku value into the mibc file, and we can take it from there (making sure we emit the new value as well as parse and validate it aot compiler).

I believe you can look at both the regular RuntimeInformation event (currently it's not fired in every session, but there might be intention to do that in the future) and the corresponding RuntimeInformation runtimedown event. Pick any of the two, but the rundown event should be present in all sessions requested rundown events (that is what dotnet-trace requests).

The full event name of the rundown event is `Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntimeRundown/Runtime/Start` where the first part is the provider and the second part is the event name. Normally you can parse it using the rundown provider in TraceEvent, there is an event there, but since it looks like its already parsed by dotnet-pgo, so just getting it by using event name Runtime/Start should match any one of the events, regardless provider.
So I assume the current impl is correct as is, right? it does poll "Runtime/Start" event and extract Sku so once Mono is added we're all set
Is anything treating the sku as a bit set? Seems like it shouldn't be.

@jakobbotsch I'm not sure what the main rationale is between making something a bitmap vs a valuemap, but this might be why its behaving as such https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/4a63cb28b69e1c48bccf592150be7ba297b67950/src/coreclr/vm/ClrEtwAll.man#L611
